repair:integrity.found: The previous engineer on this task (same KEY, repair-integrity) had done almost all of it before being stopped. In the code: names and addresses printed by full_name and email fields count as sender wording (printsName, printedWords, printedView, seenView, askView, signedOverName). A finished signer's fields are never written by a correction, so what they emptied stays empty. Quick Correct, hand-over and "Fix my name" refuse a printed name change once someone has finished. newerVersion() raises edit_version in correctRecipient, reassignRecipient, renameSelf and sendEnvelope. clearAnswers runs on every hand-over. GET /sign/:token returns sha256 per document, and the signing page keys PdfDoc and TextView by it (docUrl, allOnScreen in src/components/sign/fields.ts), with Finish off until the new pages are drawn. A replaced finished signer gets "No longer needed". A signer asked to sign again keeps the copy they signed after a void, decline or expiry (keepsCopy, earlierCopy). The 9b cases are refused with 400. "ordered" left out is kept. Signers are told about a replaced file without fingerprints; .sg-top, .sn-audit-item and email lines wrap anywhere. The API description, README row and help answer were reworded to match. Tests: 12 new ones in tests/integrity.test.ts (from line 797) plus adjustments; all 27 passed when I started. Their copies of the skeptic's probes are in tests/out/repair-integrity/ (h.ts only changed so sign-up is confirmed in the same browser, as the app now requires), with before/after outputs and browser runs (ui-swap, ui-screens, ui-pending). I re-ran all nine probes on the current code: every finding showed the fixed behaviour. One check was left ambiguous: on the phone, Finish was enabled at the moment the banner appeared, which could simply mean the new pages had already drawn.

done.how: New column recipients.link_by_sender. The shared rules and words are in src/lib/bysender.ts and the server logic in src/server/bysender.ts, with small hooks in envelopes.ts. Server: a person may have a name and no address. Nothing is ever emailed to them (notifyRecipient hands off to bySenderNotice; the void and correction emails skip them). The audit line says 'Not emailed ... The sender said they would send the link themselves'. The certificate and audit name them 'Name (link shared by the sender)' (labelOf, whoIs, certName), and the identity line reads 'Link shared by the sender only'. They count toward the daily limit (reachKey 'link:<id>') and the automatic pause (reporterKey). A signature by them is never the sender's free one. A nudge by hand is refused in words. The timer's reminder goes to the sender instead ('Reminder to pass on'). The sender gets an email when their turn comes after someone else finishes. 'Not opened yet' and 'expires soon' use wording that fits. No copy is emailed at completion: the record says so and the sender's completion email tells them to pass the copy on. Correct can rename them and keep the link, or add an address, which clears the tick and emails them. Reassigning to someone with an address clears the tick. A clone keeps the tick, a template refuses it, and the fake-notice filter still applies. Things that cannot work without an address are refused at send or correction: email plus tick, copy-only role, in-person role, groups, code by email, texted link, and an Email field. The envelope page shows an own card: Show link, Copy link, QR code, WhatsApp, text message, shown while it is their turn and after they finished, with no Nudge, no 'Sent' badge and no 'Send reminder' just for them. AfterSend says 'Now send X the link yourself'. On the signing page, the done and waiting states and the question dialog never promise an email, and say that Find my documents cannot find this document. An old replaced link answers 'ask_sender'. done.item: 2. FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY: AES-256-GCM under a key made for each file, a header with format version and key id, earlier plain files stay readable, scripts/encrypt-files.mjs
done.how: src/server/filecrypt.ts holds the format and is shared by the server and the script. An encrypted file is "\0enc", version 1, an 8-byte key id (an HMAC of the key, which says nothing about the key), a 16-byte salt, a 12-byte nonce, a 4-byte header check, then the contents and the GCM tag. The key for each file is HKDF-SHA256 of the server's key with the salt and the file's name. The header and the name are part of what GCM checks. Every write goes to a temporary file, is flushed to the disk, then renamed into place in one step. Plain files written before stay readable. scripts/encrypt-files.mjs, for each file: encrypts it into a hidden temporary file, flushes it, reads it back and checks it with the current key and the fingerprint, checks that the original has not changed since it was read, then renames over it. It has --check and --new-key, reads .env.local and .env as the server does, allows one run at a time (a lock left by a run that was killed is taken over), clears half-written copies left by an earlier run, and names damaged files and files under keys it does not have, leaving them as they are. Exit codes: 0 when done, 1 when something needs a look, 2 when a setting is wrong. How to make a key (openssl rand -base64 32) is in .env.example, the README and the script.

(stopped after the copy is written and after it is checked), 'the script keeps the original when the copy does not read back...', 'the script from the command line...'

done.item: 3. Changing the key: FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEYS_OLD and re-encryption by the script
done.how: FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEYS_OLD is a list separated by commas or spaces, and files under a listed key are read. The script moves them to the current key. An entry that is not a key is named in the log and stops nothing by itself. With only an old key listed and no current key, new files are stored as they are and the old ones stay readable; that is how encryption is switched off. There is no script that decrypts files.

(bad entry in the old list)

done.item: 4. Nothing lost by a mistake with the key: loud at start, no new files written until the old key is listed, damaged files reported and never served, no key works as today
done.how: At start, instrumentation.ts calls fileStoreWarning(), which reads the first 45 bytes of every stored file. If any file was written with a key the server does not hold, or FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set to something that is not a key, it logs 'STORING FILES IS STOPPED' with the key ids (never the keys), files an alert in the operator queue and emails SUPPORT_EMAIL and OPERATOR_EMAILS. From then on every write answers 503 "storage_stopped" with plain words that nothing was saved and nothing is lost; reads go on wherever they can. A correction that asks someone to sign again also waits with 503, because otherwise the copy of what they signed would be lost (one line in correctEnvelope). Signing still finishes, and the timer makes the signed PDF once files can be stored again. A file under a key nobody listed that turns up after the start stops writes from then on. An uploaded file that only looks encrypted cannot cause a stop: a file whose bytes match its own name is always plain. Every read checks the file, plain or encrypted. A damaged file answers 500 "file_damaged", a file whose key is missing answers 503 "file_locked", and each damaged or missing file is reported once (log, queue, email). The export leaves an unreadable signed PDF out and names it in README.txt. Storing a file that is already there with the same contents replaces a damaged copy. The warning also says what to do if a key is lost for good. With no key and no encrypted file in the folder, behaviour is as before, apart from the new check on reads and atomic writes.

I looked at both pages with my dev server at 390x844 and 1280x900, with the key on and off: no horizontal scroll and the text reads correctly. build:encrypt.notes_for_integrator:
Changes others will notice:
- Every read of a stored file is now checked against its SHA-256 name, with or without a key. A missing or changed file used to throw ENOENT or be served as it was. Now it answers HttpError 500 {code:'file_damaged'} in plain words, and a one-time alert goes to the operator queue (support_requests row named 'Sign&Grow (automatic alert)'), to the log, and by email to SUPPORT_EMAIL/OPERATOR_EMAILS.
- Writes are atomic (temporary file, fsync, rename). Storing contents that are already there now reads the existing copy and replaces it if it is damaged.
- While storing is stopped, a correction that asks someone to sign again answers 503 storage_stopped and saves nothing.
- At start the server reads the first 45 bytes of every stored file. I have not timed this on a very large folder.

Decisions the owner should confirm:
- A server with no key, finding encrypted files it cannot read, also stops storing files. That is stricter than "no key means as today", but otherwise new plain files would be mixed with files nobody can open, while the operator may believe everything is encrypted.
- I added no row to "What the bad reviews taught us". research/complaints.json has no complaint about encryption at rest, and I would not invent one.

For the rename pass:
- The constants in src/server/filecrypt.ts ('stored file key id', 'stored file v1 ...', the magic bytes) contain no product name on purpose: changing any of them would make every encrypted file unreadable. The test file checks this.
- The alert name 'Sign&Grow (automatic alert)' now appears in filestore.ts as well as routes-support.ts and routes-billing.ts. All three must be renamed together.
- The new copy says Sign&Grow where it names the product.

Left open:
(1) On the signing page, the document viewer in src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx shows its generic "The document could not be opened here... download it" for a locked or damaged file. The Download button then gets the 503/500 JSON. Showing the server's message there would need an edit in that busy file.
(2) The server never removes its own half-written temporary files (.<sha>.w<pid>-<hex>) left by a crash; only the script clears them, once they are an hour old.
(3) Running the script while the server runs leaves a tiny window in which a file the server deletes could come back encrypted. A check before the swap narrows it, and the README and the script say to stop the server first.
(4) There is no decrypt script, and the database is never encrypted (by design; documented).
(5) Someone with write access to the disk could stop storing by dropping a fake file, but with disk access they already have everything.
(6) The email to operators is sent through a dynamic import('./mail.ts'). The tests confirm it under node, but in next dev only the branch without an operator address was seen.

Screenshots and Playwright scripts are in tests/out/build-encrypt/. My dev server is stopped, .next-build-encrypt is deleted, and I removed the tsconfig lines it added. The two '.next-gaps-mobile-sign' lines now in tsconfig.json belong to another engineer and I left them.

done.item: 1. QR generator of our own in src/lib/qr.ts, proven with an outside decoder
done.how: Kept the existing encoder: I found no bug in it. I redid the outside check that was missing, in a scratch folder outside the project (nothing added to package.json). I rendered 343 codes to pixels: every version 1 to 40 (full, least and middle fill), every link length from 1 to 300, odd characters (UTF-8, right-to-left scripts, emoji, script tags, control characters), real-looking signing and form links, and every mask on 8 versions. jsQR read all 343 byte for byte. OpenCV read 278 correctly, could not find 65 (large versions), and read none wrongly. python-qrcode drew exactly the same matrix for all 343 at the same mask. Nayuki's reference encoder, choosing its own mask, drew exactly our matrix for all 279 codes where we picked the mask, so mask scoring and choice match the reference. segno differs on codes with filler bytes only: in byte mode the end mark always lands on a byte boundary, and segno 1.6.6 then adds one extra zero byte. repair:pay-core.notes_for_owner:
Changes in behaviour:
(1) When the payment provider says a plan is set to end, the plan is now worked out from a fresh read of the subscription, which costs one extra call. If the provider says the payment is failing or the new month is unpaid, the plan ends today and the waiting invoice is withdrawn. This also covers a plan the customer had already cancelled to run to the end of its month: once a payment fails, the plan ends today, under the same reference, and the email says "Cancelled earlier." If the fresh read shows the end was undone in the meantime, the message is ignored.
(2) After the provider's own message has already ended a plan, a second press of Cancel answers 400 "There is no monthly plan on this account...".
(3) An invoice that was unpaid at the moment the provider confirmed a stop is never kept if it is paid later. The exception is when the customer then presses "Pay the open payment" on purpose. Markers live in stripe_events (after-stop:, cancel-by:, doubt:) and are cleared after 60 days. A payment made before the stop is judged by status_transitions.paid_at.
(4) A card charge is never matched to one of our payments by amount alone. When the provider cannot confirm the match, an operator alert goes out and nothing is changed. This needs Stripe's invoice expand[]=payments to work; see the README test line.
(5) New refund status 'manual' ("needs a person") after three clear refusals.
(6) Wording: I wrote "you were charged after the plan was cancelled" instead of your example "you were charged after you cancelled". Mine is also true when a dispute or a closed account ended the plan. Change owedWhy() if you prefer yours.
(7) A reminder counts as delivered through the other payment engineer's mailLeft(). In development that means sent or outbox. In production, outbox counts only with DEV_OUTBOX=1, which is stricter than your "sent or outbox".
(8) Refund offers count welcome and code signatures as used first (paidAvailable). The README choices line now says so.
(9) Mail transport now gives up after 10, 10 and 20 seconds by default. This applies to every email, not only billing ones. It is documented in README and .env.example.
(10) pay-open now also offers an 'uncollectible' invoice. I am about 70 percent sure Stripe lets those be paid; there is a README test line for it.
(11) I edited two sentences in src/app/help/page.tsx (not in my file list) so the refund promise stays true.
(12) I updated existing tests billing2, billing3 and billing4. Their fake provider now shows the end it announces in the message, and billing3's "failing and set to end" case now expects the plan to be ended by the provider's message.

Still open: billing mails are still sent inside serial(), now bounded by the timeouts. A10 (a restored backup refunds unmatched payments after three days if nobody reads the first alert) is unchanged. All of the README test-mode lines still need Stripe test mode.

repair:pay-terms.notes_for_owner:
Changes in behaviour and promises:
- A new subscription is on the price its checkout showed. That price is stored on the provider subscription as metadata sg_price_cents, and an earlier notice is cleared.
- Every account gets price_cents at start (fillPrices in db.ts migrate, from the last plan payment minus tax, or the new-customer price). Deploy this before changing PRICING.

- person_gen (new recipients column) makes another person at the same address pay. A typo round trip of an address after someone signed (A to A' and back) is now charged once more.
- The Plan page badge for an on-hold plan now says 'On hold'.

New columns: payments.checked_at, recipients.person_gen, form_waits_at, form_ready_at.

Decisions still open, also in the README: whether customers keep stop-by-card without an email address (it cannot tell who is asking), and the monthly cap for free self-signing.

done.item: 1. Time-based codes and setup under Settings
done.how: New file src/server/twostep.ts has HOTP/TOTP (6 digits, 30 seconds, SHA-1) and base32, written with node:crypto, plus all the rules. Routes are in the new src/server/routes-twostep.ts. Setup: POST /me/two-step/setup asks for the password, or for a sign-in in the last 15 minutes if the login has no password. That stops someone with an unattended signed-in browser from putting their own phone in front of the login. It shows the secret as a QR code (src/lib/qr.ts), as text and as an otpauth link. POST /me/two-step/confirm switches it on only after a right code; one step either side counts for clock drift. Then 10 recovery codes are shown once, with a plain warning and Copy, Save as file and Print. Only salted fingerprints are stored, and each code works once. Switching it on signs out every other browser and emails the person. Screens: src/components/TwoStep.tsx and src/app/app/settings/TwoStep.tsx, placed under Settings, Profile.

done.item: 2. Second screen at sign-in, remember device, replay, lockout, what each answer reveals
done.how: signInAs now holds every sign-in for the second step (holdForSecondStep). It gives no session, only a waiting sign-in tied to that browser by an HttpOnly cookie for 10 minutes. The new page /login/two-step finishes it through POST /auth/two-step. Google and Microsoft redirect to that page too. For a login with two-step on, a wrong password gets the same second screen as the right one. After a code, both get the same words and use up the same 5 tries, so neither step tells a guesser whether the password was right. A code works once: the step of the last code used is stored, with an atomic update so two browsers sending the same code at once cannot both get in. 5 wrong codes in a row pause that login's second step for 15 minutes; the message says so in words, and the owner is emailed with whether the right password came first. 'Remember this device for 30 days' sets a cookie named per login. Settings lists those devices under 'Devices that skip the second step' and can withdraw them. On a remembered device a wrong password is simply 'does not match'.
done.test: 'after the password a second screen asks for the code, and a wrong password gets exactly the same answer'; 'a code works once, also when two browsers send it at the same moment'; '5 wrong codes pause...'; 'a waiting sign-in ends after its minutes'; '"Remember this device" skips the second step in that browser, for that login only, and can be withdrawn'

done.item: 3. Losing the phone: recovery codes, reset by an admin, reset by email
done.how: A recovery code signs in, and the answer and first screen say how many are left. New codes need a current code and replace the old ones. An owner or admin can reset a member's second step: POST /account/members/:id/two-step/reset. It asks for the admin's own code if they have two-step on, emails the member at once, and records who did it. The record stores only the admin's name and login id; their address is looked up while that login exists. An admin cannot reset the owner, a member cannot reset anyone, and nobody can reset someone on another team. Reset by email, for owners: 'I lost my phone and my recovery codes' on the second screen (or under Settings) emails the login's address. An owner gets a 1-hour link to /two-step-reset, a page that only starts the reset when a button is pressed. Someone who owns no account is told by email which admins can help. The answer on screen is the same after a wrong password, and then nothing is emailed. The reset takes effect 3 days later. The timer (twoStepTick in cron.ts) emails every day and switches it off on the day; a sign-in on that day applies it too. A sign-in with a code or a recovery code stops it, and so does Stop under Settings. The rules are said where it is switched on (TWO_STEP_LOST in policy.ts), on the second screen and on /help.
done.test: 'a recovery code signs in once and says how many are left...'; 'an owner or admin resets a member's second step...' (also 404 across teams and that no address is stored); 'the only owner resets by email: it takes effect after the wait, is emailed every day, and signing in stops it'; 'a reset whose day has come takes effect at the next sign-in...'; 'someone who owns no account is told by email which admins can reset it...'

build:twostep.notes_for_integrator:
Behaviour changes others will notice:
- signInAs(c, u, invite, o?) now returns {two_step: true, minutes, paused_until} and creates no session when the login has two-step login on. Any new caller must handle that answer; routes-signin.ts already does.
- POST /auth/login for a login with two-step on answers a wrong password with 200 {two_step: true} instead of 401. This is on purpose, so the password step reveals nothing. A remembered device still gets 401.
- publicUser and GET /me now carry two_step. POST /me/password and POST /me/email need "code" when two-step login is on. The router refuses routes for a person who lacks two-step login in an account that requires it (403 two_step_setup).
- An admin reset of a member is the admin's decision. The dialog says to confirm by phone or in person, but nothing enforces it.

Decisions the owner should confirm:
- After a wrong password, wrong codes count towards the login's 15-minute pause. Someone without the password can therefore keep a login's second step paused. They could already lock an address out with the existing 10-attempts-per-15-minutes password limit, and the owner is emailed each time.

done.item: 3. Find my documents, reminders, not-opened alert, declining, reassigning, access codes, bounces, abuse limits: decisions
done.how: Decisions. FIND: a member finds their own link while nobody has taken it on; after that it is found only for the person who has it. REMINDERS: go to each member who can still act, but not to one who turned them off or whose address bounced; once someone has it, only to them. NOT-OPENED ALERT: one alert per group, naming the group; quiet once any member opens. DECLINE: any member of a signer or approver group can decline; that puts them on record as having taken it on 'in order to decline it' and closes it for all; the others are emailed; the dialog says so first; a refused decline takes nothing on. REASSIGN: refused for a group; hand back instead, and the sender changes members with Edit envelope. ACCESS CODE: one for the whole group, each member types it, and wrong tries count for the group. BOUNCES: a member's bounce does not mark the group; the sender is told whose address it was and to fix it with Edit envelope (new bouncedMember in groups.ts, a small edit in routes-bounces.ts); no more reminders to that address. ABUSE: each member emailed counts as a person reached (on send and when a correction adds members); hand back 3 a day per recipient; take-over asks 2 a day per member; groups of at most 20 and 200 per account. COMPLETED COPY: goes to the person who acted and to the sender. Other members' links say who signed. In a copy group every member gets the copy. SECURITY CODE: each member's code names that member. ONE-TIME CODE OR TEXT: refused for a group.

done.how: New tables comment_threads, comments and comment_news in SCHEMA (src/server/db.ts). They are deleted with the envelope. Who reads what is decided in one place, src/server/comments.ts (sees(), threadsOf()). A private thread belongs to a person, not to a recipient row: partyOf() uses person_gen, or the member id for a signing group. So whoever takes a place over later (hand-over, corrected address, another group member) never sees the earlier person's thread and is never emailed about it. Someone else's private thread answers 404 with the same words as one that does not exist. Pins: document_id, page, and optional x/y given as fractions of the page, all checked. The signing page offers a page choice; exact x/y only through the API. Routes are in src/server/routes-comments.ts, which is imported in tests/helpers.ts and in src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts. A recipient whose turn has not come cannot read or write comments yet.

done.item: 2. Telling people: the sender gets at most one email every 10 minutes per envelope with the comments in it; a recipient gets one when the sender answers them; the guards on sending (assertMayEmail, the pause, the fake-payment-notice filter) apply
done.how: Each comment writes one comment_news row per person to be told. flushComments() sends one email per envelope and person, with everything new in it, unless one went to them in the last COMMENT_MAIL_MINUTES (10). What waits goes with the next comment or the timer (added to src/server/cron.ts tick). Checking and marking as sent happen in one step with no wait in between, so nothing is sent twice. Who is emailed about a sender's-side comment: the person a private thread is with, or, in a thread for everyone, each person who wrote in it. A new thread for everyone emails nobody, and the sender is told so in words. Sender's-side text calls emailRefusal() (not a copy): it is refused with 422 when it reads like a fake payment notice, and nothing is saved. At send time emailRefusal() is asked again; while the account is paused the answer waits and goes out after the pause is lifted. Someone with no address, signing in person, who marked our email as spam, whose address bounced, or whose place passed to someone else is not emailed, and the sender sees why on the envelope page and in the API answer. Recipient emails carry their own link and security code. The sender's email sets a reply address only when one person with an address wrote, and says that such a reply is not kept with the document.

- An unclaimed signing group cannot be written to privately; the sender writes for everyone instead.
- Recipients' comments for everyone are not run through the fake-notice filter. They are never emailed to the others, only shown on their signing pages, and public-form visitors cannot write for everyone.
- An answer to an address that bounced is dropped for good, not resent after the address is corrected.
- Waiting emails go out with the next comment or the next timer run: every 15 minutes in-process, or whenever CRON_SECRET's scheduler calls.
- The burst limits are in memory like other rateLimit uses. The 50 limit is in the database.

doubts_about_outside_services: Google hd: Google's own guidance treats email_verified plus a gmail.com address, or the presence of hd, as Google being authoritative for the address. I am fairly sure (about 80%) that a Workspace or Cloud Identity address is always in a domain that org verified, so the hd-mismatch case should not occur with real tokens. There have been public reports of Workspace sign-ups usable before domain verification, but I cannot confirm whether hd was ever issued then. I cannot call Google.

Microsoft xms_edov: I am moderately sure (about 70%) that it is an optional ID-token claim set in Token configuration or the manifest's optionalClaims, and that Microsoft omits unverified email claims by default for newer multi-tenant apps. Either way the code fails safe (unvouched means our confirmation email). I do not know whether personal (MSA) accounts ever carry xms_edov:true.

Microsoft key list: apps that use a claims-mapping policy (custom signing keys) must fetch the JWKS with ?appid=<client id>. Optional claims alone do not need this, as far as I know. If an operator adds a claims-mapping policy, every Microsoft sign-in fails with 'failed'.

Endpoints, issuers (accounts.google.com in both spellings; login.microsoftonline.com/{tid}/v2.0, including the personal tenant 9188040d-...), PKCE with a confidential web client, response_mode=query and prompt=select_account all match what I know of both providers (high confidence). Nothing was run against the live providers; my browser run aborted every request that left localhost.

__Host- cookies depend on x-forwarded-proto reaching the app. If a host terminates TLS without sending it, c.secure is false, the server sets sg_signin_note without the prefix, and the landing page (on https) only reads __Host-sg_signin_note, so the first-screen notice (joined, reclaimed, linked) is silently lost. Render sends the header, so this is probably fine there.

new_bugs.title: Timer retry of a link text ignores everything since the first try: texts the OLD wrong number after a correction, a disowned number, a reporter, a paused sender, someone who already signed
new_bugs.where: src/server/sms.ts tooLate() and retryTexts(); src/server/signercode.ts resetCheck() only expires kind='code' texts (dropCodeTexts)
new_bugs.detail: Probe tests/out/verify-signercode/retry.ts, Twilio stubbed, first provider answer 503 so the 'link' text is failed with next_try_at. (1) POST /envelopes/:id/correct {recipient_id, phone:'+44 7700 900112'} -> 200; make the old text due; cron.tick -> texts {sent:1}; Twilio called with To=+447700900111, the number the sender just said was wrong, body 'Sign&Grow, sent for Ada Sender: "Wrong number corrected" is waiting for you to sign. http://test.local/sign/<token>'. With text_link and no code check, whoever holds that number can open and sign. (2) after POST /sign/:token/code/problem {what:'not_mine'} the retry still texts +447700900121. (3) after POST /sign/:token/report the retry texts the reporter. (4) after the account is paused the retry goes out. (5) a signer who finished (other signer pending) is texted 'is waiting for you to sign'. Fix: in tooLate load the recipient by recipient_id and drop the text when to_phone differs from normalPhone(recipient.phone), text_link is off, check_stop is set, status is completed or declined, muted (reminders), an abuse report exists, or emailRefusal(e) refuses; and expire all queued or failed texts of a recipient (not only codes) whenever the number, the person or the check changes and on not_mine.

new_bugs.title: Another person at the same inbox inherits the first person's passed code, and the certificate says they passed it
new_bugs.where: src/server/signercode.ts linkStamp/deviceStamp (keyed on recipient id and token only); src/server/envelopes.ts correctRecipient sameInbox branch and writeContent otherName (keep the token, bump person_gen)
new_bugs.detail: Probe certificate.ts #3: Sam Smith (email_code) passes the code on his device. POST /envelopes/:id/correct {name:'Alex Jones', email: same} -> 200; same token, person_gen 1, consent cleared (the app treats Alex as another person). Sam's device: GET /sign/:token locked=false. API check: {line:'One-time code sent by email to c***@example.com, passed 20 November 2026 19:30 UTC', passed_at: Sam's time}. Alex finishes from that device; certificate for Alex Jones: 'Identity check One-time code sent by email to c***@example.com, passed 20 November 2026 19:30 UTC'. Alex never typed a code. The comment in signercode.ts says a pass stops counting when the address is corrected to another person, but this path keeps the link. Fix: include person_gen in linkStamp and deviceStamp, or call resetCheck whenever person_gen changes.

new_bugs.title: A stranger (another account, or an anonymous public-form visitor) can use up a mailbox's 15 codes a day and lock that person out of every sender's document for 24 hours
new_bugs.where: src/server/signercode.ts requestCode, SIGNER_CODES_PER_DESTINATION_DAY counted over all accounts by dest_hash
new_bugs.detail: lockout.ts #2: Mallory's account sends 15 envelopes with email_code to victim@, asks for a code on each -> Hana's genuine envelope to the same address: POST /sign/:token/code -> 429 '15 codes have gone to v***@example.com in the last 24 hours, which is the most we send to one mailbox in a day. Try again tomorrow.' #3: no account at all: 16 POST /public/powerforms/:slug/start with the victim's address from 16 addresses -> all 200; 15 'Your code to open a document from Hana HR' emails land in the victim's inbox; the victim's real document then answers 429. Fix: count the destination limit per account (or per envelope) with a far higher global ceiling; count a public form's code emails against that form's visitor limit and limit starts per address; never let codes from one account block another account's signer.

new_bugs.title: 15 codes an hour per internet address locks out an office signing a bulk send
new_bugs.detail: lockout.ts #1: 16 colleagues, each with their own email_code document, all behind 203.0.113.77 -> statuses 200 x15, then 429 '15 codes were asked for from your internet connection in the last hour'. find() in routes-sign.ts already says one address can be a whole office signing a bulk send. Fix: count per (address, account) or only count codes that ended in wrong tries; rely on per-recipient and per-destination limits for flooding.

new_bugs.title: A paused account keeps texting numbers it typed by opening its own links and asking for codes
new_bugs.where: src/server/signercode.ts requestCode -> mayText (no pause or fake-notice check)
new_bugs.detail: paused.ts: unpaid account sends 3 envelopes with sms_code to 3 numbers and its own email, is paused (suspended_at), gets each link with POST /envelopes/:id/recipient-view (200) and asks for codes from rotating addresses: 15 texts '... is your Sign&Grow code to open a document from Mo Sender ...' go out while paused. The author's test asserts this on purpose ('a code ... still works while paused'), but the sender can be the one asking. Fix: refuse code texts while the account is suspended (neutral words to the signer, tell the sender), or at least when the request comes from a browser signed in to the sending account.

new_bugs.title: A link holder who never passed the code can silently switch off the signer's texts
new_bugs.where: src/server/routes-sign.ts /sign/:token/mute and /report use find(c, false); signercode.ts alsoText returns silently on a report
new_bugs.detail: stranger.ts #3: without the code, POST /sign/:token/mute -> 200 and /report {reason:'not-for-me'} -> 200. Next day's reminder: texts before 1, after 1; audit shows 'Reminders stopped' and 'Reported as suspicious' but no 'Text not sent', and the sender is not told texts stopped. Fix: require the code check for /mute when verify is a code; when a report stops texts, write 'Text not sent' and tell the sender once.

new_bugs.title: 'This is not my number' stops texts for that one link only
new_bugs.where: src/server/signercode.ts codeProblem sets recipients.check_stop; mayText/textRefusal never look at other recipients
new_bugs.detail: notmine-scope.ts: not_mine on envelope 1 for +447700900432; the same sender's envelope 2 to the same number a minute later gets a link text and a code (texts: ['link','code']). The help page says 'We stop texting it at once, codes and links alike'. Fix: keep a stop list per account (or global) by phoneKey, refuse a send to it in words until the sender confirms.

new_bugs.title: Our stored copy of a code email keeps the code when it was sent on a timer retry
new_bugs.where: src/server/signercode.ts requestCode redacts only when the first try is 'sent'; src/server/mail.ts retryMail/deliver never redacts
new_bugs.detail: mailretry.ts: SMTP stub throws '451 try later' on the first try -> signer gets 502; cron.tick -> mail {sent:1}; emails row status 'sent' and html still contains the 6-digit code. README says the stored copy loses the code once the mail server has taken it. Fix: redact rows with expires_at after any successful try (or store the code only as a placeholder rendered at send time).

new_bugs.detail: dialog.cjs at 390x844: label 280x44, checkbox 7x13 (flex shrinks it when the text wraps), select text 'One-time code by text messag' cut off. new_bugs.title: Before the code, the envelope id in the locked view plus the public lookup reveal the other people's count and progress and the page count
new_bugs.where: src/server/signercode.ts lockedView keeps envelope.id and impact; src/server/evidence.ts lookupEnvelope
new_bugs.detail: lookup.ts: locked view gives envelope.id and impact.sheets 9; GET /public/verify/<that id> -> {status:'sent', signers:2, signed:0, approvers:1, pages:{documents:3}, sent_at}. Fix: leave id and impact out of lockedView (the code screen does not use them).

new_bugs.title: Pass cookie is one fixed value per link and never expires on the server
new_bugs.detail: stranger.ts #6: two devices that passed get the identical cookie value; a copied cookie opens the link on a third client after checked_at was moved 3 days back. README: 'stays passed for that link for a day'. Fix: sign an issued-at into the cookie and refuse it after 24 hours.

new_bugs.title: Code screen tells a 'link shared by the sender' person that 'The link in your email keeps working'
new_bugs.detail: certificate.ts #2: a link_by_sender recipient with sms_code (no email) can press 'I do not get the code' (200); the told note then says the link in their email keeps working, but they have no email from us. Fix: use env recipient link_by_sender to say 'The link you were given keeps working'.

new_bugs.title: Premium-rate and international-network numbers are accepted for texting
new_bugs.detail: race.ts #6: '+1 900 555 0100', '+44 909 879 0000', '+882 1234 5678', '+881 6 1234 5678', '+999 1234 5678' all normalise and would be texted; a sender can then ask for codes on their own links (up to 200 a day per account). The builder names this as left open. Fix: refuse +881/+882/+883/+888/+979 and known premium ranges, validate with libphonenumber, optional SMS_COUNTRIES allow list.

new_bugs.title: Per-caller code limit is off or spoofable depending on TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS
new_bugs.where: src/server/router.ts clientIp; src/server/signercode.ts requestCode skips the caller limit for 'unknown'
new_bugs.detail: Code reading: TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=0 makes every ip 'unknown', which requestCode does not count at all; the default 1 on a server with no proxy takes the caller's own X-Forwarded-For, so each request can name a new address (the tests themselves do exactly this). Fix: say in README that the caller limit needs a correct TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS, and fall back to a per-recipient-and-account bucket when the address is unknown.

overclaims.reality: A correction to another person at the same address keeps the link, so the new person inherits the pass and the certificate says they passed (certificate.ts #3).

overclaims.reality: The line is 44 px but the checkbox itself is 7x13 px at 390 wide and the select text is clipped, visible in the builder's own 21-phone-confirm-number.png.

overclaims.claim: 'Not my number' stops all texts to that number, now including link texts. Tested. / Pause and the fake-payment-notice filter are re-checked at the moment of every link text.
overclaims.reality: Not on timer retries, and not across envelopes; pause not checked for code texts.

overclaims.claim: a refusal for good (a number that does not exist) ends at once
overclaims.reality: With Twilio a well-formed but unassigned or landline number is normally accepted (201) and fails later through status callbacks the app never asks for, so it is recorded as 'sent' and the sender is not told (see doubts).

overclaims.claim: 15 an hour per caller address ... Tested (as protection)
overclaims.reality: The same limit refuses the 16th colleague of an office behind one address (lockout.ts #1), and the 15 a day per mailbox can be used up by another account or an anonymous form visitor (lockout.ts #2, #3).

doubts_about_outside_services: Twilio request shape: POST https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages.json, application/x-www-form-urlencoded with To, Body and From or MessagingServiceSid, Basic auth AccountSid:AuthToken, 201 with a JSON sid. This matches Twilio's long-stable Messages API; I am about 90 percent sure, from the documented API, not a live call. API key auth (SK sid + secret) is not supported by this code, which is fine because the settings ask for the account SID and auth token.

Twilio acceptance is not delivery: unassigned numbers, landlines and carrier-filtered messages usually return 201 and fail later (errors 30003, 30005, 30006, 30007) via StatusCallback, which the code never sets. So the app records 'sent' and never tells the sender; the 'I do not get the code' button is the only fallback. About 75 percent sure about which failures surface at API time (21211 invalid format, 21610 opted out, 21408 country not enabled, 21614 not a mobile all come back as 400 and are correctly final).

Duplicates: a 15-second timeout after Twilio actually accepted the message leads to a second send on the timer; the Messages API has no idempotency key. Low cost, same code in both, but counts once in sms_usage and twice on the bill.

Segments: with a 40-character sender name and a normal host the code text is about 180 GSM-7 characters (2 segments); any non-GSM character in the sender's name (for example 'ë', Polish or any CJK) switches to UCS-2 at 70 per segment, 3 or more segments. SMS_DAILY_PER_ACCOUNT counts messages, not segments.

The last line '@host #code' matches the WebOTP / origin-bound one-time code format (must be the last line, host without port), which the code does. Fairly sure; Android Chrome honours it, iOS reads the code from the text anyway.

Generic hook: POST JSON {to, text} with Authorization: Bearer is exactly the contract the brief defines, so it is what an adapter written for it expects. It accepts http:// URLs, which would send the token, numbers and codes in clear text, and any 2xx is taken as sent with no later failure path.

Premium-rate numbers: Twilio blocks premium-rate destinations and limits countries by Geo Permissions by default (fairly sure); a hook provider may not, and this code accepts +1 900, +44 909, +881/+882 and unassigned country codes.

checks.item: An account that is not trusted cannot get a Pay button shown by any route (API, template copy, bulk, public form, correction, envelope made while trusted and shown after trust was lost, refund or dispute)
checks.evidence: PUT /envelopes/:id/pay-link refuses with 403 without trust (author test 21, and my probe). Every copy path (copyEnvelope for template use, /clone, bulk rows, public forms) copies pay_url, but GET /sign/:token/pay and POST pay-opened call payRefusal(e.account_id) at show time. probe-pay.ts: a public form visitor of a trusted account sees the link; probe-refund.ts: an account trusted only by a 40-day-old payment shows the link, then after refunded_cents=200 on that payment (the same write routes-billing.ts line 317 does) GET /sign/:token/pay returns pay:null. Pause, dispute and trusted mark removal are covered by author test 23. No other code path writes pay_url (grep).

checks.item: Addresses that lead somewhere else are refused: javascript:, data:, every spelling, invisible characters, punycode
checks.evidence: checkPayUrl parses with WHATWG URL and requires protocol https:, so JAVASCRIPT:, data:, https:buy.stripe.com, backslash tricks all normalise or are refused. Invisible characters the regex misses (U+00AD, U+FE0F in the host, U+2066/U+2069 and U+3164 in the path) are either dropped by IDNA or percent-encoded in the stored href, and the screen and button show only the href and the ASCII/xn-- host, so what is displayed is what opens. probe-pay.ts results: 'https://pay­pal.com/x' stored as https://paypal.com/x; 'https://paypal.com/⁦x⁩' stored as https://paypal.com/%E2%81%A6x%E2%81%A9.

checks.item: 'A host that is not on the public internet' is refused
checks.evidence: probe-pay.ts, checkPayUrl(url, 'sign.example.org') accepts https://192.168.1.1.nip.io/admin, https://127.0.0.1.sslip.io/, https://localtest.me/, https://localhost.localdomain/pay, https://router.home.arpa/, https://nas.alt/ and https://*.example.com/. The check is by name only (LOCAL regex), never by what the name resolves to at set time or at show time.
checks.still_broken: A trusted sender (or a stolen trusted login) can point the Pay button of every signer at the signer's own router admin page or another private address.
checks.suggested_fix: Refuse the reserved suffixes (home.arpa, alt, localdomain, arpa) and the well-known wildcard-DNS services (nip.io, sslip.io, xip.io, localtest.me, lvh.me); at PUT time and at GET /sign/:token/pay resolve the host (dns.lookup all) and refuse any private, loopback, link-local or CGNAT address; or reword the claim to 'a host whose name says it is not public'.

checks.item: The signer sees 'the exact address it leads to'
checks.evidence: probe-pay.ts: https://bit.ly/3abcdEF, https://tinyurl.com/pay-now, https://t.co/abc, https://www.google.com/url?q=https://evil.example.net/pay and https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=... are all accepted. pay.cjs at 390x844: the button reads 'Pay the deposit on bit.ly' (screenshot sign-pay-bitly-phone-full.png). The length refusal even tells senders to 'Use the short link your payment provider gives you'.
checks.still_broken: The named host is not where the money goes; a stolen trusted login can use a shortener so the audit trail and the screen show only bit.ly.
checks.suggested_fix: Refuse a list of known shorteners and redirectors (bit.ly, tinyurl.com, t.co, goo.gl, ow.ly, is.gd, buff.ly, rebrand.ly, cutt.ly, lnkd.in, l.facebook.com, www.google.com/url, href.li), refuse any URL whose query or fragment contains http, https%3A or // (after decoding once), and change the 500-character message so it no longer recommends short links.

checks.item: Anything over 500 characters is refused
checks.evidence: probe-pay.ts: 'https://pay.example.com/' + 470 Cyrillic letters is 494 characters and is accepted; the stored and displayed href is 2844 characters (maxIsOnInputOnly.storedLength=2844). The length is checked on the raw input, not on u.href.
checks.suggested_fix: Check u.href.length (and the host length) against PAY_URL_MAX after parsing.

checks.item: The link is never put in our emails
checks.evidence: probe-attach.ts with SMTP_URL set: the 'Completed: Mail cert' emails to ana-m (signer), kit-m (cc, never asked to pay) and the sender each carry the attachment 'Mail cert.pdf'; pdfjs text of that attachment contains https://buy.stripe.com/mail_cert. probe-pay.ts pdfSnippet from the cc's download: 'Payment link added · "Pay the deposit" opens https://buy.stripe.com/gus_cert_deposit. It is shown to each person who signs, after they finish, and never in an email.' The certificate prints every audit line (pdf.ts drawCertificate loop), including 'Payment link added/changed', 'Shown the payment link' and 'Opened the payment link'. Author test 22 only scans emails.html, never the attachment.
checks.still_broken: A sender-typed payment address goes out in our completion email, under our name, to every recipient including copies and approvers; the audit line in the same PDF even says 'never in an email'.
checks.suggested_fix: Print payment-link audit lines in the certificate without the address (for example 'Payment link added (address kept in the audit trail, ending in its host buy.stripe.com)') or with the address defanged (hxxps, spaces around dots), or leave those lines out of the PDF and keep them in the online audit trail and evidence pack; then add the attachment text to the test.

checks.item: The link never appears in a webhook body
checks.evidence: webhooks.ts fireWebhooks builds the body from SELECT id, status, subject, sent_at, completed_at plus the caller's extra; no pay_url or audit detail. Webhooks go to the account's own endpoint in any case.

checks.item: The signing link does not leak to the payment site
checks.evidence: pay.cjs at 390x844: the button has rel='noopener noreferrer' and referrerpolicy='no-referrer' and opens target=_blank. GET /sign/:token after Finish does not carry the address (signPageCarries=false). I did not observe the Referer header at a real destination; browsers honour rel=noreferrer, high confidence.

checks.item: Shown only after Finish and only to people who sign
checks.evidence: Before Finish and for approvers and copies it is null (author test 22). But probe-pay.ts senderAskedToPayThemselves: when the sender Gus is a signer of his own envelope, GET /sign/:token/pay for his own link returns the card 'Gus Builder asks you to pay here ... If you did not expect to pay Gus Builder anything, do not pay', and records 'Shown the payment link' for him. Same for the account owner who countersigns a public form (formOwnerAskedToPay = https://buy.stripe.com/booking).
checks.still_broken: The sender, or a colleague from the same account, is asked to pay their own deposit, and the sender's record counts them as shown.
checks.suggested_fix: In GET /sign/:token/pay and POST pay-opened, return nothing when the recipient's address belongs to a member of the envelope's account (or equals the sender's email).

checks.item: A change after completion is refused; once completed or closed the link can only be removed
checks.evidence: PUT with a new url on a voided envelope answers 409 (author test 23). But probe-pay.ts section 7: the sender deletes a completed envelope (DELETE answers kept_for_recipients:true, hidden_at set); the signer still gets the Pay card (delSignerStillSees=https://buy.stripe.com/del_dep) while GET and PUT /envelopes/:id/pay-link for the sender both answer 404, so the sender can no longer even remove it. Only an admin restoring the envelope can.
checks.still_broken: A sender who deletes an envelope (for example because the deal fell through after signing) cannot stop signers being asked to pay.
checks.suggested_fix: Hide the link (pay:null) for envelopes with hidden_at set, or clear pay_url in DELETE /envelopes/:id when it only hides the envelope, with an audit line.

checks.item: The record of who was shown it and who pressed it is accurate
checks.evidence: probe-pay.ts section 5: Ana was shown and pressed https://buy.stripe.com/old_link, then the sender changed the link to https://evil-but-trusted.example.net/new while the envelope was out. GET /envelopes/:id/pay-link (the envelope page) still says Ana shown_at and opened_at with the old timestamps under the new link; recipients.pay_shown_url and pay_opened_url still hold the old link; Ana was emailed nothing. Section 11: POST pay-opened with no prior GET answers recorded:true and the page shows 'not shown yet ..., pressed on ...'. Section 3: after the envelope was voided, GET /sign/:token/pay returns null but POST pay-opened still answers recorded:true and writes 'Opened the payment link ... was sent on to https://buy.stripe.com/void_dep'. By code, a middle click or long-press 'open in new tab' fires no onClick, so the page says 'not pressed yet' for someone who did open it.
checks.suggested_fix: Return shown_url and opened_url with the times and show 'shown the earlier address X' when they differ from pay_url; reset pay_shown_at and pay_opened_at when the url changes (keep history in the audit trail); in pay-opened require the same status check as GET and that pay_shown_url equals pay_url; record on auxclick too, and word the sender's line as 'not recorded as pressed'.

checks.item: The signer sees the sender's name with the link
checks.evidence: probe-pay.ts section 8: member Max sets https://paypal.me/maxpersonal on his envelope and sends it; the owner removes Max (DELETE /account/members/:id, envelopes handed to the owner); after the signer finishes, the card says senderNameShown 'Olga Owner', senderEmailShown 'olga-v@example.com' with Max's personal PayPal link. Nothing in the hand-over touches pay_url or writes an audit line about it.
checks.still_broken: A removed member keeps collecting deposits through the team's envelopes, under a colleague's name.
checks.suggested_fix: In handOver (or on member removal) clear pay_url on the envelopes and templates that move, with an audit line and a line in the hand-over email, or store pay_set_by and show that person's name and refuse to show it once they left the account.

checks.item: Shown correctly on a 390x844 phone with no sideways scrolling
checks.evidence: pay.cjs: with a valid 462-character link whose host is 150 characters (pay.securesecure....checkoutcheckout....example-payments-provider.com, accepted with 200), the signing page scrollWidth is 1301 at clientWidth 390 and the button is 1268 px wide; 'Pay the deposit on' sits off screen to the right and only the host is visible (sign-pay-long-phone.png). The <code> block wraps fine because it has break-all; the button has only white-space:normal. Short links are fine (scrollWidth 390).
checks.suggested_fix: Give the button overflowWrap:'anywhere' and wordBreak:'break-word' and maxWidth:'100%', or cap the host length (for example 100 characters) in checkPayUrl.

checks.item: Two requests at the same moment write one line each
checks.evidence: probe-pay.ts section 10: two GET /pay and two POST pay-opened in Promise.all leave exactly one 'Shown the payment link' and one 'Opened the payment link' audit line (the handlers are synchronous after find()).

checks.item: A team member cannot change a colleague's template link; an API key does what a login does
checks.evidence: Author test 24 (403 for a member); probe-pay.ts section 12: a send-scope API key sets a link (200) on its owner's envelope, as a login would. Groups: asMember's MAY table lists neither 'pay' nor 'pay-opened', so only the member who took the document gets the link (read in groups.ts).

checks.item: Reminders on by default for new accounts and said before every send
checks.evidence: probe-rest.ts: a new account has default_reminder_days 3, an envelope made by the API without reminder_days gets 3, a new template 3. But an account from before (default 0) sends a bulk batch from its template: the envelope goes out with reminder_days 0, and neither the bulk page nor POST /bulk/check mentions reminders (bulkCheckSaysReminders=false; grep of src/app/app/bulk/page.tsx finds no reminder sentence). The same holds for public forms. The editor review step, the envelope page and Settings do print reminderText.
checks.suggested_fix: Print reminderText(template.reminder_days) on the bulk page next to BatchCost (and return it from /bulk/check), and on the public form settings; or narrow the claim to 'before every send from the editor'.

checks.item: POST /bulk/check shows the numbers POST /bulk is held to
checks.evidence: probe-rest.ts with credits on: check for 3 rows says need 3, have 3, short 0; two POST /bulk of 3 rows at the same moment: one sends 3, the other is refused 402 'This needs 3 signatures and you have 2 left'. Both use batchNeeds. Edges seen: a row that is the sender under their own name and address is counted as 1 although sending it alone costs 0 (checkOwnRow need 1), and via the API 600 rows are reported as rows 500, need 500, cost $497 while POST /bulk refuses 'Send up to 500 envelopes per batch' (the page itself caps at MAX_ROWS 500).

checks.item: Filled in everything but has not pressed Finish (progress.ready) and the reminder wording
checks.evidence: Author tests 14 and 15 pass. probe-rest.ts: ready turns true for a required checkbox saved as '0', 'false' or 'off', but POST /complete also accepts '0' for that required checkbox (200), so ready matches what the server lets finish. checks.item: F: a dispute never deletes anything and the mark stays for the envelope's life

checks.suggested_fix: Treat disputed_at like a signature in DELETE /envelopes/:id (hide only, never forgetEnvelopes). Add a disputed_at column to forgotten_files, fill it in keepFingerprint, and return it from forgottenFile and lookupEnvelope so both /verify answers keep saying 'Disputed'.

checks.item: F: the person who disputes is told truthfully what the sender learns

checks.item: F: the dispute screens say the right thing about who is told

checks.item: D: 'Completed copy opened ... for the first time' is true

After a first download, setting it back to NULL (the state of every pre-existing row) and downloading again writes a second line 'Sam Signer downloaded the completed document for the first time, in Chrome on a Windows computer.' Every person who downloaded before deployment will get a false 'first time' line in the live trail.
checks.suggested_fix: In the db.ts migration, set copy_opened_at (to completed_at or a sentinel) for recipients of envelopes already completed, and for those write 'opened the completed document (first time since this was recorded)'.

checks.evidence: Code: single UPDATE ... WHERE copy_opened_at IS NULL and WHERE COALESCE(visit_noted_at, viewed_at) < dayAgo decide; author tests D2/D3 cover reloads and the next day. Not re-proved concurrently by me beyond reading.

checks.item: E: a voided, declined or expired copy can never pass for a signed one
checks.evidence: probe2 + render-pdf.cjs: voided envelope with Ada's signature and date at the lower right (x 0.6, y 0.84). voided-2.png shows the diagonal mark and the signature block do not touch; threshold.cjs counts 0 mark pixels in the lower-right corner. The mark is red at opacity 0.24 (grey level 212 at its darkest): after a 50% black-and-white threshold (a copier or fax in text mode) 0 of 19743 mark pixels remain and the small 'NOT COMPLETED BY EVERYONE' line vanishes too (voided-2-bw.png). probe1 P8: a copy the sender downloads while the envelope is still out shows Ada's signature with no mark at all; voiding later does not change that file.
checks.still_broken: Crop the lower-right quarter, or photocopy in black and white, and the signed block is clean.
checks.suggested_fix: Draw the mark as repeated rows tiled over the whole page (both diagonals), at opacity 0.45 or more in a dark colour, draw 'VOIDED' inside or beside every signature and initials field in drawField, repeat the small line at top and bottom, and mark copies downloaded while out with 'NOT COMPLETED YET'.

checks.item: G: the evidence pack holds nothing that is not the sender's business and no live keys

Comments are threadsOf(e, {side:'sender'}), which are threads the sender is already in. Help acknowledgements and the operator dispute email are sent without envelopeId, so they are not in the pack. API key with the send scope gets it (P11: 200).

checks.item: H: the certificate page says nothing the certificate and marks do not do

'Sender: the login that sent it' is wrong after handOver, which rewrites sender_id on envelopes still out, so the certificate names the heir (read from code, not probed).

overclaims.reality: completed_at is kept and published to the millisecond (e.g. 2026-11-20T19:37:29.540Z).

overclaims.claim: 'Completed copy opened' marks the first time each person opens the completed copy.
overclaims.reality: For every recipient already in the database the first download after deployment is labelled 'for the first time' whatever they did before (P2).

doubts_about_outside_services: Black-and-white copies: the 50% threshold models a copier, fax or scanner in text or bilevel mode. Many devices in greyscale or photo mode would keep a light grey mark, so I am fairly sure but not certain the mark disappears on real office copiers; the corner crop finding does not depend on any device.
Forwarded completion emails: whether recipients forward them (to a landlord, bank, colleague) is user behaviour I cannot measure; the code in the email is confirmed (P4).

Mail link scanners: 'Completed copy opened' and 'Opened again' can be written by a scanner that runs JavaScript on the /sign page; I could not test a real scanner. The completion email's button points at the page, not the download, which lowers the risk.

The dev server reloaded many times while other engineers edited files (signing page and /check took several tries to render); that looked like work in progress elsewhere, not a fault of this piece. Final passes rendered every screen.

brand:growsigner.kerning:
I added one kerning pair and kept the two existing ones. The kerning sits on top of Lora's own kerning (GPOS: r-o -8, o-w -8), in thousandths of an em, in EXTRA_KERN in scripts/build-brand.mjs.

- e-r: -8 (new). To check spacing I measured the white area between each pair of letters across the x-height, with the depth of open counters capped at 100 units. Lora sets e-r at 161. The other pairs in "signer" measure n-e 154, s-i 153 and i-g 151, so e-r is 7 to 10 units looser. At 200 px this shows as a gap before the final r. With -8 it measures 153, and a 200 px render shows it even with n-e.
- r-o: -6, kept. I compared 0, -6 and -10 at 200 px. At 0 the space under the r's arm opens up. At -10 the r's ball terminal crowds the o. -6 is right.
- w-s: -10, kept. I compared -10 and -4 at 200 px. Both are clean. -10 holds the colour break between "grow" and "signer" together, and the letters around this pair are the same as in growsigning.
- Left alone: n-e, s-i and i-g, which are even with each other. g-n measures open (178), but the g's ear fills the top of the gap. It is the same as before and matches g-r in "grow" (also 178), so I left it.
- At 22 px each of these moves is under 0.2 px. They change how the word looks large, not whether it reads small. Renders at 22 px at 1x and 2x look clean.

brand:growsigner.decisions:
What was done:
- The kit now carries "growsigner". scripts/build-brand.mjs now has the word, its 4+6 split and the kerning in one place (WORD, SPLIT and EXTRA_KERN), and every master and title is built from WORD. I ran `node scripts/build-brand.mjs --masters`, then rebuilt again after the guide edits.
- Renames: the keys `signing` become `signer` in TONES and LOGO in src/lib/brandMark.ts. Brand.tsx now uses LOGO.signer and t.signer, and its default accessible name is "growsigner". Nothing in src imports either file yet, so nothing breaks.
- README: name table and never-list; files table (stamp text, email logo 266 by 44 at 133 by 22); a new proportions table; the smallest-sizes table with widths and the e note; the colour table; the three kerning pairs under Type; the don'ts; a new section "The rename, from growsigning to growsigner"; licences. In Wiring it in: alt text, a 133 px email img, LOGO.signer in the PDF snippet, manifest name and short_name 'GrowSigner', "Sent with GrowSigner", and a fresh count of Sign&Grow (315 in 78 files).
- guide.html: every name, example and caption; an "On the web: growsigner.com" row; the ratios; widths in the size table; and a new real-pixel enlargement of logo.svg at 16 px. I looked at guide.png and at every SVG and PNG at real size on their own grounds.
- brand/concepts was left untouched (git shows no change there).
- I made no git changes. However, something else in this repo makes automatic "work in progress by the engineers" commits (4ff8174, e84faf5, 8bfd156). Those commits picked up in-between states of these files while I worked. The final versions are in the working tree and will go into the next such commit.

For the owner to decide:
1. All capitals. I kept GROWSIGNER on the README's never-list, carrying over the old guide's ban on GROWSIGNING, although the brief wrote the name in capitals for emphasis. Confirm all caps is never allowed. For example, the guide's own small uppercase labels must avoid the name; I took the domain out of one for that reason.
2. Files outside this task's scope that still say "growsigning". Each needs a one-word change by whoever owns it:
   - the first-line comment in src/app/styles/brand.css
   - the Lora comment in scripts/copy-assets.mjs
   - tests/encrypt.test.ts line 695, whose regex /Sign&Grow|growsigning/i should probably also match growsigner.
3. g-n and g-r are slightly open by measurement, as they were in growsigning. I left them so as not to change "grow". Say if you want both tightened together.
4. The relayed user question, "can you not use my existing Render subscription?", is unrelated to this brand task, and this step did not answer it. Someone should take it up separately.
